title: Where Have You Been? A Study of Privacy Risk for Point-of-Interest Recommendation

problem.claim: Mobility data used by location-based services and their machine learning models can leak sensitive information about user identities, including home and work locations.

gap.claim: Prior work protects mobility data during transmission or before release but does not evaluate the privacy risks of mobility-data-based machine learning models.

contributions.claim: A privacy attack suite is designed for point-of-interest recommendation models, combining data extraction and membership inference attacks.
The attack suite covers different adversary knowledge assumptions and targets different types of sensitive information to assess privacy risks in a holistic way.
The study examines which types of mobility data are more susceptible to privacy attacks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their findings about which types of mobility data are more susceptible to privacy attacks as unique.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two real-world mobility datasets demonstrate that current point-of-interest recommendation models are vulnerable to the proposed attacks.
The authors evaluate defenses against the attacks and identify future directions and challenges.

narrative_sequence.summary: The growth of location-based services has increased the collection of human mobility data, which supports machine learning models for improved service performance and user experience.
Using mobility data creates privacy-leakage risks because the data may contain sensitive identity-related information.
Existing privacy protection work does not evaluate privacy risks in mobility-data-based machine learning models.
The study introduces a tailored attack suite for point-of-interest recommendation models with varied adversary knowledge and sensitive-information targets.
Experiments assess model vulnerability, susceptible mobility-data types, and defenses against the attacks.

source_observation.claim: Privacy assessment should account for attacks with different adversary knowledge and information targets.

interpretation.claim: A multi-scenario attack suite can provide broader risk coverage than evaluating a single threat model.

application.claim: When assessing privacy in machine learning systems, vary attacker assumptions and define the sensitive information each attack seeks to recover.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this approach is sufficient for all mobility-data-based models or privacy threats.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two datasets, model architectures, attack implementations, or quantitative results.
The effectiveness and conditions of the evaluated defenses are not reported.
The abstract does not identify the specific mobility-data types found to be more susceptible.
